contextNote: Ran as an independent adversarial pass with no authoring context: I read the repository from scratch (src/policy.ts, src/path-mapper.ts, src/workspace-path.ts, src/routing-guard.ts, src/host-runner.ts, src/host-run-ledger.ts, src/tools.ts, src/commands.ts, src/execution-service.ts, extensions/index.ts, src/runtime/host-discovery.ts, docs/security.md, CHANGELOG.md), drove the freshly built dist/src modules through inline node -e harnesses (no repo file was modified; /tmp writes are denied by this session's permission policy, so the harnesses ran in-memory), and re-ran the recorded gates myself instead of trusting the evidence list.

attempts.hypothesis: AC-1 + docs/security.md: a credential can reach the operator surfaces ONLY when spelled as a program name with no '@' or '/' at all (docs/security.md:174-176); the ledger/status line renders no credential.
attempts.method: Generated tokens embedding a marker credential around '@' and '/' and ran them through displayProgram and through createHostRunLedger/status summary (dist build).
attempts.evidence: displayProgram(["alice:Pq7@Xr2Zm9K"]) => "Xr2Zm9K"; displayProgram(["https://user:Pq7@Xr2Zm9K/db"]) => "Xr2Zm9K"; end-to-end: ledger.record(["postgres://alice:Pq7@Xr2Zm9K"]) then ledger.recent() => ["Xr2Zm9K","docker"] and ledger.summary() => "2 host command attempts this session — most recent: Xr2Zm9K | docker" (that string is what /devcontainer status prints). A fuzz over 16 token wrappers x 3 injection points produced 22 tokens where ≥5 chars of the credential survive.

attempts.hypothesis: AC-1: a credential-free path keeps its basename (and the revision's own claim that a Windows path renders `docker.exe`).
attempts.method: Called displayProgram on Windows/UNC/POSIX program paths.
attempts.evidence: displayProgram(["C:\\tools\\docker.exe"]) => "C"; displayProgram(["C:/tools/docker.exe"]) => "C"; displayProgram(["d:\\a\\b\\c.exe"]) => "d"; while UNC and POSIX keep the basename ("\\\\server\\share\\docker.exe" => "docker.exe", "/usr/bin/docker" => "docker"). The drive-letter authority is mistaken for a `user:password` authority, so the drive letter is rendered as the "username".

attempts.hypothesis: AC-1: control AND format characters are stripped (commit claims the strip set is now 'Cc + Cf').
attempts.method: Called displayProgram with C1 controls, C0/DEL, Cf and invisible non-Cf code points.
attempts.evidence: displayProgram(["docker\u009b2J"]) => "docker\u009b2J" (code points 64,6f,63,6b,65,72,9b,32,4a — U+009B survives); U+0085 survives. The regex is [\u0000-\u001f\u007f\p{Cf}] = C0+DEL+Cf, i.e. NOT the whole Cc category (C1, U+0080-U+009F). Invisible non-Cf fillers also survive: "tool\u3164\u3164", "tool\uffa0x", "tool\u115f" are unchanged (Cf does strip: "tool\u200b" => "tool", U+202E removed).

findings.message: displayProgram can still render credential material, so the ledger stores it and /devcontainer status prints it — contradicting AC-1's 'NO command text is stored or rendered', the CHANGELOG's 'without creating a place a credential could be rendered', and docs/security.md:174-176 ('A credential can therefore only reach the operator surfaces by being spelled as a program NAME with no @ or / at all'). When the credential itself contains an '@' and nothing follows the last '@', the rule 'the userinfo is the text before the LAST @ and everything after it is the host' returns password text: displayProgram(["alice:Pq7@Xr2Zm9K"]) => "Xr2Zm9K", displayProgram(["https://user:Pq7@Xr2Zm9K/db"]) => "Xr2Zm9K" (rule 4 of redactText cannot cross the userinfo and only strips up to the first '@', leaving the tail to be re-read as the host). End-to-end: createHostRunLedger().record(["postgres://alice:Pq7@Xr2Zm9K"]) then recent() === ["Xr2Zm9K", ...] and summary() === '2 host command attempts this session — most recent: Xr2Zm9K | docker' — a password remainder, not a program name. A fuzz over 16 token wrappers x 3 injection points produced 22 such tokens (up to 10 of 10 credential chars). Honest framing: under WHATWG-URL reading of the original token the leaked fragment sits in the host position, so the renderer's output is defensible for e.g. 'https://user:a@b/db' (userinfo user:a, host b) — but that defense does not hold for the doc's absolute claim, and a caller-intended DSN with an '@' in the password and no path ('postgres://alice:p@ssw0rd') leaks the whole tail. Fix is either to stop applying the '@'-rule to a token that carries a ':' before any '@' (render '(no command)' instead) or to correct the doc sentence.

A Windows drive-letter program path loses its basename, contradicting AC-1's 'a credential-free path keeps its basename' and this revision's own stated result ('`C:\tools\docker.exe` → `docker.exe`'). The authority `C:\tools\docker.exe` contains a ':' whose tail is not all digits, so authorityLooksLikeUserinfo is true and the code renders the USERNAME (the drive letter) instead of the basename: displayProgram(["C:\\tools\\docker.exe"]) => "C", displayProgram(["C:/tools/docker.exe"]) => "C", displayProgram(["d:\\a\\b\\c.exe"]) => "d". UNC and POSIX paths are unaffected ("\\\\server\\share\\docker.exe" => "docker.exe", "/usr/bin/docker" => "docker"). Effect: on a Windows host the operator notice and /devcontainer status name 'C' instead of the tool that ran (no credential impact — a degraded/incorrect operator signal). A drive-letter test would have caught it; tests/unit/routing-guards.test.ts:352-358 only covers POSIX and `@babel` paths.

The strip is not the 'Cc + Cf' set the revision claims, and it is not complete for what a name can carry. The regex is /[\u0000-\u001f\u007f\p{Cf}]/gu = C0 + DEL + Cf, so the C1 control block U+0080-U+009F (category Cc, i.e. control characters) survives: displayProgram(["docker\u009b2J"]) => "docker\u009b2J" (observed code points 64,6f,63,6b,65,72,9b,32,4a), U+0085 survives too. Invisible non-Cf code points also survive and can still pad/spoof the name the operator is asked to trust: "tool\u3164\u3164" (HANGUL FILLER), "tool\uffa0x" (HALFWIDTH HANGUL FILLER), "tool\u115f" (HANGUL CHOSEONG FILLER) are rendered unchanged, while U+200B and U+202E are correctly removed. Impact is low (operator-channel text only, UTF-8 terminals do not treat C2 9B as CSI), but the stated strip set and AC-1's 'control AND format characters stripped' are both inaccurate — '\p{Cc}\p{Cf}' plus the Default_Ignorable set would match the claim.

The same-path (mirror) mount exemption and the guard's variable expansion support only the braced '${localWorkspaceFolder}' spelling, while the extension's own expander (expandLocalWorkspaceFolder, src/path-mapper.ts:57-63) explicitly supports the bare '$localWorkspaceFolder' form for the workspaceMount source — the 'one surface fixed, its mirror not' defect class this review established. Reproduced: config {workspaceMount: 'source=${localWorkspaceFolder},target=/workspaces/p,type=bind', mounts: ['source=<SPELLING>,target=/data/ws,type=bind']} — with the braced spelling readConfigFacts yields samePathMounts ['/data/ws'] and detectHostPathOnContainerSurface(['cat','/data/ws/README.md'], mapping) === undefined (allowed); with the bare spelling samePathMounts is undefined and the same, legitimate request is refused with policy-denied 'container command references the HOST path'. Effect: a false-positive refusal in a workspace that mirror-mounts its own path using the legacy spelling; both src/path-mapper.ts (samePathMounts) and src/routing-guard.ts (expandVariables) omit the bare form.
